author: WP19
summary: Surveys what the 20 workflows actually run (portable, browser, platform, Apple/Windows, C API, Content Pipeline, diagnostics, sanitizers, fuzzing, coverage) and how to report CI. The verification and testing-architecture pages already had the per-workflow table; the trigger facts, non-ASCII Windows content lane, diagnostics/Inspector reach, GPU-validation and fuzzing specifics and the reporting fields are new on the verification-tiers reference. The Wayland lane and the diagnostics coverage claims were corrected.

sections.heading: C API and Content Pipeline gates

concepts.text: No workflow executes the full cross-product of OS, platform, renderer, audio, features, compiler and device; TARGET has 20 workflow files, all startable manually and 18 with push or pull-request triggers (usually path-filtered), and a workflow file proves intent, not that a run completed or every conditional job engaged.

The general Linux job builds tests and examples and runs CTest with an expected-failure classification; input and devices have focused matrices and sanitizer selections; the 32-bit job runs arithmetic programs, not a 32-bit CNA; the glTF stride and sanitizer jobs have oracles narrower than a model-rendering campaign.
tokens: a classification step allows exactly one known, tracked failure

concepts.text: HTML_DOM is the strongest automated browser route (served page, real Chromium, verdicts, compositor pixels); the Emscripten multi-renderer job proves a compatible bundle, not every renderer's browser pixels, and the native multi-renderer job proves descriptor generation and early runtime selection for a CPU and diagnostic set.
tokens: The multi-renderer lane establishes configure/build/link, not browser behaviour

concepts.text: platform-ci.yml treats platform, renderer and audio as independent axes with SDL3/SDL2/headless/terminal cells, SDL-free X11 lanes, a MinGW Win32 job under Wine and a manual native-MSVC Win32 job; the claim of a native Wayland lane is corrected: no workflow covers Wayland.
tokens: No workflow covers native Wayland or Android

target.evidence: .github/workflows/platform-ci.yml (jobs: platform-contract, win32-cross, win32-native, x11-sdl-free, x11-sdl-free-gpu, sdl-enable-matrix)

concepts.text: Live Weston, Mutter, XKB, text-input, clipboard, pointer and portal suites are registered under the environments they need and skip where those are missing; a missing compositor, display or input method is not a passing behaviour test.

Apple and Metal workflows do not imply iOS or tvOS devices or every GPU; the Direct3D and GDI workflows are manual-only; native MSVC, MinGW under Wine with DXVK, WARP and a physical interactive Windows machine remain different evidence tiers.

concepts.section: C API and Content Pipeline gates
concepts.text: Five build-free C API workflows cover declaration/export coverage, pure-C compiler compatibility, the ABI baseline, limitation records and the release decision; the checked-in gate reads "Not ready" (one unmet criterion), and the coverage generator refuses unclassified modules, so checked-in counts must not override executions (the unit's "two unmet criteria" is its own reproduction, not re-run here).
tokens: All five are build-free header and inventory checks

concepts.section: C API and Content Pipeline gates
concepts.text: The Content Pipeline has a native Windows MSVC workflow that builds the CLI and CPU pipeline and exercises it from a deliberately non-ASCII fixture path, catching path, encoding and packaging assumptions a Linux build cannot; a green build-time tool is not runtime content proof.

Claim that Diagnostics OFF/STATS/FULL code is covered through compile and unit configurations: no workflow or preset sets CNA_DIAGNOSTICS above OFF or CNA_BUILD_INSPECTOR, so CI compiles only the level-independent diagnostics tests and no Inspector test; neither subsystem has a workflow.
Generated XNA API, renderer registry, platform containment, module closure and content inventories are structural proof, not behavioural parity.
tokens: are structural proof, not behavioural parity

concepts.text: ASan and UBSan appear in focused input, glTF and devices lanes and GPU validation is family-specific (Vulkan and OpenGL4 output gates, Direct3D debug layers, Metal validation variables, WebGPU error scopes) and must prove its own engagement; a sanitizer-clean CPU route cannot establish a native driver's state or pixels.

Fuzz-named GoogleTests are deterministic adversarial loops; libFuzzer entry points exist for the compiled-effect, model and intermediate-format harnesses and two C API sources, but no workflow runs a continuous libFuzzer or AFL campaign.
tokens: no workflow runs a continuous fuzzing campaign
concepts.note: Nuance: the unit says the tree has no campaign; entry points exist but are not run.

concepts.text: Direct2D mutation dry-run anchor validation is weaker than rebuilding and killing every mutation, and no workflow configures gcov, lcov, gcovr or llvm-cov, so files named coverage describe inventories rather than measured line, branch or function coverage.
tokens: No workflow configures gcov, lcov, gcovr or llvm-cov

concepts.text: An honest CI statement names the workflow and run, trigger, commit, matrix tuple, built targets, selected tests, skips, the engagement token and artifacts; "covered by CI" is too coarse because browser pixels, a manual native run, a generated ABI baseline and a registry comparison prove different things.

issues.text: No coverage instrumentation exists in any workflow or CMake option; the only line-coverage figure is a hand-recorded single-module report.
libFuzzer/AFL harnesses are neither CTests nor run by any workflow.
Vulkan, Software and DirectX11 glTF L7 goldens and the WebGPU/SDL_GPU/OpenGL4 parity-fixture CTests are recorded or registered but run by no workflow.
